domain: Perioperative crises & complications (malignant hyperthermia, anaphylaxis, local anesthetic systemic toxicity, cannot-intubate-cannot-oxygenate, intraoperative awareness, massive hemorrhage, air/PE embolism, cardiac arrest)
stem: Anaphylaxis is mediated by what immunologic reaction and presents with what hallmark features?
answer: Type I (IgE-mediated) hypersensitivity; presents within minutes of antigen exposure with acute respiratory distress, circulatory shock, or both.
rationale: IgE on mast cells cross-links with antigen causing degranulation; vasoactive mediators cause simultaneous airway and cardiovascular collapse.
confusable_with: Anaphylactoid reaction (not IgE-mediated, same clinical presentation)

domain: Perioperative crises & complications (malignant hyperthermia, anaphylaxis, local anesthetic systemic toxicity, cannot-intubate-cannot-oxygenation, intraoperative awareness, massive hemorrhage, air/PE embolism, cardiac arrest)
stem: What mediators from anaphylaxis produce upper vs lower airway obstruction?
answer: Upper airway: angioedema of pharynx/larynx/trachea causes obstruction. Lower airway: bronchospasm + mucosal edema (leukotrienes, prostaglandins).
rationale: Both pathways threaten oxygenation but through different mechanisms; epinephrine is first-line as it reverses both vasodilation (alpha) and bronchoconstriction (beta2).

domain: Perioperative crises & complications (malignant hyperthermia, anaphylaxis, local anesthetic systemic toxicity, cannot-intubate-cannot-oxygenate, intraoperative awareness, massive hemorrhage, air/PE embolism, cardiac arrest)
stem: What is the mechanism of refractory hypotension in anaphylaxis and what third vasopressor is added?
answer: Coronary hypoperfusion + vasodilation; vasopressin added if hypotension is refractory to norepinephrine plus epinephrine.
rationale: Massive vasodilation from multiple mediators can overwhelm catecholamine support; vasopressin acts via V1 receptors independently of adrenergic pathways.

domain: Perioperative crises & complications (malignant hyperthermia, anaphylaxis, local anesthetic systemic toxicity, cannot-intubate-cannot-oxygenate, intraoperative awareness, massive hemorrhage, air/PE embolism, cardiac arrest)
stem: Why is epiglottitis considered a differential in acute severe airway symptoms in adults?
answer: Acute epiglottitis (commonly H. influenzae) causes rapid progression from sore throat to dysphagia to complete airway obstruction; endotracheal intubation + antibiotics can be lifesaving.
rationale: Adult epiglottitis has increased as an important diagnosis since vaccination reduced pediatric cases; supraglottitis involves all supraglottic structures.

domain: Perioperative crises & complications (malignant hyperthermia, anaphylaxis, local anesthetic systemic toxicity, cannot-intubate-cannot-oxygenate, intraoperative awareness, massive hemorrhage, air/PE embolism, cardiac arrest)
stem: In anaphylaxis, what leukotriene and prostaglandin-mediated complication can occur at the coronary level?
answer: Coronary vasospasm; leukotriene and prostaglandin mediators can cause coronary vasospasm contributing to myocardial ischemia in anaphylaxis.
rationale: Combined hypoperfusion from hypotension plus coronary vasospasm creates high risk of arrhythmias and MI during severe anaphylaxis.

enabling_conditions: Prior sensitization to allergen (antibiotics, latex, neuromuscular blockers, contrast, foods); occurs within minutes of exposure
pathophysiology: IgE-mediated mast cell/basophil degranulation releasing histamine, tryptase, leukotrienes, prostaglandins, bradykinin -> simultaneous vasodilation, bronchoconstriction, and increased vascular permeability
time_course: Onset within minutes; death from asphyxiation or irreversible circulatory shock possible within 30-60 minutes if untreated
key_features: Urticaria/angioedema + bronchospasm + hypotension; tachycardia; absent features do not exclude diagnosis
consequence_if_missed: Irreversible cardiovascular collapse and death; airway angioedema can make intubation impossible
